a dresser must be flush against a wall (.rule: A dresser must be flush against a wall (back on wall); the solver must snap it to the wall within tolerance.

a nightstand must not overlap a bed; the.rule: A nightstand must not overlap a bed; the solver must reject a placement that causes a collision.

a bed must have at least 0.60 m free alo.rule: A bed must have at least 0.60 m free along its sides; the solver must reject a placement that does not meet this clearance.

a wardrobe's front use zone must be reac.rule: A wardrobe's front use zone must be reachable by a 0.60 m walkway from the room's door; the solver must reject a placement that blocks that path.

a shower must not stand in front of a wi.rule: A shower must not stand in front of a window (blocking the opening); the solver must reject a placement that blocks a window.

a floor lamp must not stand in front of.rule: A floor lamp must not stand in front of a window sill; it is placed beside the seating, not between the seat and the glazing.

a bathtub's back must sit on a wall; a 2.rule: A bathtub's back must sit on a wall; a 2 cm offset is a placement slip, not a tolerance.

a washbasin's back must sit on a wall; a.rule: A washbasin's back must sit on a wall; a 7 cm offset is a placement slip.

a washing machine's front use zone must.rule: A washing machine's front use zone must be reached by a 0.60 m walkway from the room door.

the exterior environment must be a belie.rule: The exterior environment must be a believable, textured setting (ground, trees, path) for a client presentation, not a flat untextured plane with crude low-poly trees.
The exterior environment must be a believable, textured setting, not a flat featureless green plane with lollipop trees.

every opening cut through a wall must be.rule: Every opening cut through a wall must be built with its frame and head/sill (a door with a frame and a window with a frame and sill), never as a raw unframed hole with a floating bar.

an armchair belongs in a seating arrange.rule: An armchair belongs in a seating arrangement, not pushed flat against a wall under a window.

the view outside a window must show a be.rule: The view outside a window must show a believable, textured site, not a flat untextured plane with crude trees.

a piece the decor stage placed must surv.rule: A piece the decor stage placed must survive the agent stage; if the agent drops it, the next round must restore it.

a stove must be built as its own object,.rule: A stove must be built as its own object, not as part of the kitchen_counter module; if the scene has no object for it, give it a real stove model.

a fridge must be built as its own object.rule: A fridge must be built as its own object, not as part of the kitchen_counter module; if the scene has no object for it, give it a real fridge model.

a label that names a furniture type in a.rule: A label that names a furniture type in a room with no piece at its anchor is a missing piece and must be added, not dropped.

a drawn cluster larger than 4.5 m on a s.rule: A drawn cluster larger than 4.5 m on a side is a group of pieces, not a single untyped piece; it must be split and typed, not marked not-furniture.

a room outline that holds two labels (e..rule: A room outline that holds two labels (e.g. Salon and YEMEK BÖLÜMÜ) is a wall not read; the second label is a dining zone that must be given its own dining group, not merged into the living room.

the upper end of a stair that arrives at.rule: The upper end of a stair that arrives at a level must be built at that level; it is not dropped because 'no level above'.

drawn strokes on the furniture layer tha.rule: Drawn strokes on the furniture layer that no piece uses are lost pieces (a sofa, chairs around a table) and must be read and built.

a room outline that holds two labels (e..rule: A room outline that holds two labels (e.g. Mutfak and ANTRE) is a wall not read; the second label is a separate room that must be split out.

a door shown on an elevation must be cut.rule: A door shown on an elevation must be cut in the model's wall; the reading must carry elevation doors into the plan.

a nightstand that is a necessary piece o.rule: A nightstand that is a necessary piece of a bedroom must be built; a placement conflict is solved by re-solving the sleeping group, not by dropping the nightstand.

a labelled site area (veranda) outside t.rule: A labelled site area (VERANDA) outside the walls must be built as a site area with an outline, not kept as a site record.

a labelled site area (balkon) outside th.rule: A labelled site area (BALKON) outside the walls must be built as a site area with an outline, not kept as a site record.

a kitchen's dining table is redundant wh.rule: A kitchen's dining table is redundant when the salon has one; the kitchen must have a proper worktop arrangement (kitchen run), not a row of identical blank boxes.

a dressing room must have a dressing gro.rule: A dressing room must have a dressing group (wardrobe, mirror, bench), not a single wardrobe; the room must be lit (a window or a light) so the renders are not +9 EV.

a door on l1 must be connected to a stai.rule: A door on L1 must be connected to a stair or walkway; a door into the air (3.50 m above the ground with nothing to reach it) is a reading error.

a staircase must have handrails or balus.rule: A staircase must have handrails or balustrades on both sides; an open stair with no guard is a safety issue and a visual defect.

a room typed as a bedroom must have a be.rule: A room typed as a bedroom must have a bed; a bedroom with no bed does not read as a bedroom.

a bathroom whose usable floor area is un.rule: A bathroom whose usable floor area is under 7.0 m2 must not be furnished with a 1.80 m bathtub; the wet-room set for such a room is a shower, a toilet and a washbasin, and the layout solver must reject any bathtub placement that leaves less than 0.53 m of clear approach.

in a bathroom under 7.0 m2, the washbasi.rule: In a bathroom under 7.0 m2, the washbasin must be placed on the wall opposite the door or on a wall that leaves at least 0.53 m of clear approach; the layout solver must not place it in a corner blocked by the bathtub or toilet.

in a bathroom under 7.0 m2, the toilet c.rule: In a bathroom under 7.0 m2, the toilet centre must be at least 0.38 m from any side wall or fixture; the layout solver must enforce this minimum when placing the toilet in a crowded wet room.

the elevation check must compare the num.rule: The elevation check must compare the number of windows on each facade side in the drawing against the model, and flag any discrepancy where the model has more windows than the drawing shows.

every window and door of a room must be.rule: Every window and door of a room must be visible in at least one of the room's required camera views; when a view cannot show the required pieces, the room is re-laid out so the pieces are in a position a camera can show, and the camera is then set to show them.

a washbasin must be at a usable working.rule: A washbasin must be at a usable working height (rim about 0.85 m) and reachable; when the current model is too low or wedged behind another fixture, a model with the correct height and footprint is swapped in.

a bathroom door must not open directly i.rule: A bathroom door must not open directly into the fixture cluster; the bathroom set is solved so the door swing and the approach to the fixtures are clear.

a labelled veranda or balcony in the doc.rule: A labelled veranda or balcony in the documents must be built as a site area with an outline, slab, and railing; its absence is a loss of documented content.

a drawn cluster larger than 4.5 m on a s.rule: A drawn cluster larger than 4.5 m on a side must be split into individual pieces or typed as a group before building; it cannot be left untyped.

a named piece in the documents (e.g. a d.rule: A named piece in the documents (e.g. a dresser) must be placed at or near its text location; if the nearest valid place is more than 1 m away, the room layout must be adjusted to accommodate it.

a room whose name or drawn program is a.rule: A room whose name or drawn program is a dressing room (soyunma odası) is typed bedroom (or storage if it holds only a wardrobe and no bed), never 'other', so its program (wardrobe + mirror + seating) is checked and completed.

the ground floor's level mark (e.g. '+0,.rule: The ground floor's level mark (e.g. '+0,50' printed in the section) is the finished-floor datum of the building; the reading must set the ground floor to 0.00 m and read every other relative mark against it, not offset the whole building by the printed mark.

the big loop must not stop at the first.rule: The big loop must not stop at the first cycle when the deadline is still far off; it keeps running fix cycles until the score stops improving or the deadline is reached, so the remaining time is spent on more cycles.

when a room's program group (e.g. dressi.rule: When a room's program group (e.g. dressing) has no place that passes the checks because the room is too small or the group is too large, the solver must either place a reduced version of the group or record the room as intentionally minimal, rather than silently adding nothing.

a small drawn piece around a level-mark.rule: A small drawn piece around a level-mark text (e.g. '+0,50') is a level-mark symbol, not furniture, and must be recorded as such, not built as a piece.

views marked for review must be re-check.rule: Views marked for review must be re-checked after the fix cycle that addresses their room; if the room's furniture is unchanged, the view is re-rendered and re-scored, not left marked.

a wardrobe (or tall storage) that blocks.rule: A wardrobe (or tall storage) that blocks a door or window swing must be moved to a wall span that does not intersect the swing, or the door/window must be repositioned; the solver must not leave a tall piece blocking a swing when no free span exists, but instead flag the room layout as infeasible.

a kitchen must have its main functional.rule: A kitchen must have its main functional anchors (fridge, hob/stove, sink, counter) placed as a coherent run; if the room's geometry does not allow the full run, the solver must place a reduced run and flag the missing anchors, not leave the kitchen without a hob or fridge.

a floor lamp whose model has a shade tha.rule: A floor lamp whose model has a shade that is too large and sits at head height (blocking sightlines) must be swapped for a model with a proportionate shade and a height that does not block the room's main sightline.

a washbasin (or any fixture) that blocks.rule: A washbasin (or any fixture) that blocks a door or window swing must be moved to a position that does not intersect the swing, or the door/window must be repositioned; the solver must not leave a fixture blocking a swing when no valid spot exists, but instead flag the room layout as infeasible.

a large living room (e.g. 55 m2) must ha.rule: A large living room (e.g. 55 m2) must have its main furniture (sofa, coffee table, armchair) placed so that the main view shows them; if the room's geometry does not allow the full set, the solver must place a reduced set and flag the missing pieces, not leave the room bare.

a shoe cabinet (or any tall storage) und.rule: A shoe cabinet (or any tall storage) under a sloped ceiling must be swapped for a model that fits the available height (at most the ceiling height at that point); the solver must not leave a crude, low-poly model when a real product of the type fits within the height constraint.

the architect's rule f5 (which says cert.rule: The architect's rule F5 (which says certain overlaps are fine) must explicitly list the cases it covers (e.g. kitchen_counter overlaps of up to 0.5 m2 are fine); the critic must not flag overlaps that the rule already accepts.

the architect's rule s4 must explicitly.rule: The architect's rule S4 must explicitly state the minimum clear space in front of a bathtub (e.g. 0.53 m); the critic must not flag bathtubs that meet the rule's minimum.

the architect's rule f4 must explicitly.rule: The architect's rule F4 must explicitly state the minimum free zone in front of an armchair (e.g. 0.60 m) and which pieces may block it; the critic must not flag armchairs whose free zone is blocked by a piece that the rule allows.

a tall storage piece (wardrobe, tall_cab.rule: A tall storage piece (wardrobe, tall_cabinet, bookshelf) must not stand in front of a window whose sill is lower than the piece's top; the piece blocks the view and the light, so it must be moved or the window raised.

a sofa's free zone in front must be clea.rule: A sofa's free zone in front must be clear of other pieces for at least 0.90 m; if another piece blocks it, the sofa or the blocking piece must be moved.

a dressing room with only a wardrobe mus.rule: A dressing room with only a wardrobe must have a camera that shows the wardrobe and the room's usable space, not a bare corner.

exterior trees must be high-quality mode.rule: Exterior trees must be high-quality models, not low-poly placeholders. If the library has no good tree model, reduce the count or use a hedge instead.

a kitchen counter that cuts a wall must.rule: A kitchen counter that cuts a wall must be moved to a valid spot within the room, not left intersecting the wall.

a washbasin must have a faucet, mirror,.rule: A washbasin must have a faucet, mirror, and accessories. If the current model is bare, swap to a model that includes these elements.

a bathtub must have a shower head, fauce.rule: A bathtub must have a shower head, faucet, and accessories. If the current model is bare, swap to a model that includes these elements.

a toilet must match the room's aesthetic.rule: A toilet must match the room's aesthetic. If the current model is dated, swap to a modern model.

a kitchen counter must have handles, mat.rule: A kitchen counter must have handles, material variation, and appliance integration. If the current model is a parametric placeholder, swap to a designed model.

a living room seating group must have va.rule: A living room seating group must have variety, not four identical chairs. Swap at least one chair to a different model.

a small, untyped piece in a living room.rule: A small, untyped piece in a living room that is not built is likely a drawing artifact, not furniture. Mark it as not furniture.

a dining table must match the room's aes.rule: A dining table must match the room's aesthetic. If the current model is a plain, boxy slab, swap to a designed model.

a coffee table must match the room's pal.rule: A coffee table must match the room's palette. If the current model is a clashing wood tone, swap to a model that fits the palette.

a hall or entrance room must have an ent.rule: A hall or entrance room must have an entrance group (shoe cabinet, console, or lighting) placed; if the room is too small for a full group, at least a shoe cabinet or console table must be placed.

a stair model must match the project's s.rule: A stair model must match the project's style; if the parametric stair looks generic, a library model with a more designed railing and finish should be used.

an interior camera must show the main pi.rule: An interior camera must show the main pieces of the room; if the camera is too close to a corner or tilted, it should be repositioned to show the main furniture and the room's layout.

doors must have a frame and hardware det.rule: Doors must have a frame and hardware detail; a flat slab door without a frame or handle looks like a placeholder. The door material should be a painted wood or a textured finish.

a wardrobe model must match the project'.rule: A wardrobe model must match the project's style; if the current model is a dark, heavy carved wooden bench, a lighter, more modern model should be used.

a floor lamp model must match the projec.rule: A floor lamp model must match the project's style; if the current model is an ornate, turned-wood classic style, a more neutral and modern model should be used.

an interior camera must show the main pi.rule: An interior camera must show the main pieces of the room, including windows; if the window is not visible, the camera should be repositioned to show it.

the main entrance door must have a handl.rule: The main entrance door must have a handle, texture, or frame detail; a generic, flat white slab looks unfinished. The door material should be a painted wood or a textured finish.

window and door frames must match the pr.rule: Window and door frames must match the project's style; a generic, flat grey frame clashes with the white facade and dark roof. The frame material should be a metal or a painted finish that matches the facade.

the ground must be textured; a flat, unt.rule: The ground must be textured; a flat, untextured green plane looks like a video game. The ground material should be grass, paving, or gravel.

an interior camera must show the main pi.rule: An interior camera must show the main pieces of the room; if the camera is pointed at a blank wall, it should be repositioned to show the main furniture and the room's layout.
An interior camera must show the main pieces of the room; if the camera is aimed at a blank tiled wall, it should be repositioned to show the main fixtures and the room's layout.

a kitchen set must have appliances, cook.rule: A kitchen set must have appliances, cooktop, and styling; a flat, untextured white wall-cabinet run looks like a placeholder. The kitchen model should include a cooktop and appliances.

when a seating set in one room mixes sty.rule: When a seating set in one room mixes styles, swap the outlier to a model from the same style family as the sofa and the other chairs.

an interior camera must be posed to show.rule: An interior camera must be posed to show the room's main fixtures; when the judge says a fixture is missing from the frame, re-aim the camera at the fixtures that are actually in the room.

when a seating set in one room mixes sty.rule: When a seating set in one room mixes styles, swap the outlier to a model from the same style family as the other furniture.

an interior camera must be posed to show.rule: An interior camera must be posed to show the room's main furniture; when the judge says the frame is a dead-end wall, re-aim the camera at the furniture that is actually in the room.

a swap_model candidate for a piece under.rule: A swap_model candidate for a piece under a sloped ceiling must pass the fit rules (caps, height, at most 2.80 m high under the sloped ceiling) before being offered; if no candidate passes, the finding is left for review rather than forcing a crude model.

the exterior site must have a ground loo.rule: The exterior site must have a ground look and a reasonable number of trees; a grey void with lollipop trees is not client-ready.

an interior camera must be posed to show.rule: An interior camera must be posed to show the room's main fixtures; when the judge says the frame is a bare wall, re-aim the camera at the fixtures that are actually in the room.
An interior camera must be posed to show the room's main fixtures; when the judge says the room is missing its main anchor, re-aim the camera at the fixtures that are actually in the room.
An interior camera must be posed to show the room's main fixtures; when the judge says the kitchen reads as a broken half-built set, re-aim the camera at the fixtures that are actually in the room.

a fridge model must have door splits, ha.rule: A fridge model must have door splits, handles and brand detail; a flat silver slab is not client-ready.

an interior camera of a kitchen must fra.rule: An interior camera of a kitchen must frame the kitchen run, sink and stove, not the adjacent hall or dining table.

a dining table model must match the room.rule: A dining table model must match the room's minimal/modern style, not a crude low-poly placeholder.

a chair model must match the room's ligh.rule: A chair model must match the room's light, minimalist palette, not a dark heavy traditional piece.

a sofa model must match the room's coher.rule: A sofa model must match the room's coherent palette, not a clashing orange mid-century piece.

opposite sofas in a seating group must r.rule: Opposite sofas in a seating group must read as a coherent set, not mismatched styles and colours.

a salon's seating group must be anchored.rule: A salon's seating group must be anchored by a coffee table and rug, not two unrelated sofas facing each other on bare floor.

a salon must read as a designed interior.rule: A salon must read as a designed interior with one coherent palette, not a showroom of clashing mid-century pieces.

the exterior seen through a window must.rule: The exterior seen through a window must be a realistic landscape, not a crude low-poly cartoon of lollipop trees and flat ground.

a bathroom must show its washbasin, and.rule: A bathroom must show its washbasin, and a washing machine must not be crammed into a corner that blocks the set.

a toilet model must match the room's cle.rule: A toilet model must match the room's clean, modern lines, not a dated standard model.

the exterior seen through a window or ba.rule: The exterior seen through a window or balcony door must be a realistic landscape, not a cartoon of flat lollipop trees on flat ground.

the exterior seen through a window must.rule: The exterior seen through a window must be a realistic landscape, not a crude cartoon of flat lollipop trees and featureless ground.

an office chair model must match the roo.rule: An office chair model must match the room's calm, light palette, not a dark bulky piece.

a children's room must read as a designe.rule: A children's room must read as a designed space, not a generic low-budget bedroom with an oversized dresser blocking the window.

a bed model must be a complete, correctl.rule: A bed model must be a complete, correctly textured asset; a glossy black slab with voids is a broken model that must be swapped for a valid library model.

a bedroom's furniture set must be stylis.rule: A bedroom's furniture set must be stylistically coherent; the bed, nightstands, and any additional furniture must share a common design language.

seating in a room must be stylistically.rule: Seating in a room must be stylistically coherent; an office chair next to armchairs should match their material and silhouette family.

a bedroom must be fully furnished with a.rule: A bedroom must be fully furnished with a coherent set; missing pieces from the schedule must be added, and broken models must be swapped.

a door model must include visible hardwa.rule: A door model must include visible hardware (handle) and frame details; a plain untextured slab is a placeholder that must be swapped for a valid library model.

interior hall cameras must be positioned.rule: Interior hall cameras must be positioned to show the circulation path and key fixtures (stair, shoe cabinet) from a free point, not from an angle that exposes safety issues like an unguarded stairwell.
Interior hall cameras must be positioned to show the circulation path and key doors, not aimed at a bare corner.

a bedroom must contain a bed; if the roo.rule: A bedroom must contain a bed; if the room is furnished as a lounge, it should be retyped or the furniture should be changed to match the bedroom program.

interior cameras must be positioned to s.rule: Interior cameras must be positioned to show the room's layout and key doors, not dominated by a blank wall.

interior dressing room cameras must be p.rule: Interior dressing room cameras must be positioned to show the room's layout and the wardrobe from a free point, not pressed against the wardrobe.

decor items must rest on their host with.rule: Decor items must rest on their host without penetration; if a cushion penetrates the sofa, it should be adjusted or removed.
Decor items must rest on their host with at least 80% of their footprint over the support; if a cushion does not meet this threshold, it should be adjusted or removed.

the dwg reading stage must parse attdef.rule: The DWG reading stage must parse ATTDEF (attribute definition) entities in addition to TEXT and MTEXT entities, as architectural drawings often store room names, dimensions, and furniture tags as block attributes. Ignoring ATTDEF entities causes loss of labelled data that the model should reflect.

a tiny hall with no pieces is acceptable.rule: A tiny hall with no pieces is acceptable; its connectivity is carried by the doors, not by pieces.

a room's seating must not be four identi.rule: A room's seating must not be four identical chairs, and the front use zone must be reached by a 0.60 m walkway from the door.

the main entrance door must be legible:.rule: The main entrance door must be legible: a door leaf, handle, canopy or frame detail, not a flat slab.

a drawn piece whose type is not allowed.rule: A drawn piece whose type is not allowed in its room must be retyped to a type that fits its size and room, or removed, before the run is accepted.

when a room outline contains more than o.rule: When a room outline contains more than one room label, the reading stage must split the outline at the missing wall so each label gets its own room.

an interior camera must be posed to show.rule: An interior camera must be posed to show the room's principal pieces; if a render check reports listed pieces as invisible, the camera is re-aimed to include them.

a bed_double model must have a height an.rule: A bed_double model must have a height and proportions that read as a double bed in all views; if a render check reports it looks like a single, swap to a model with a taller frame.

a piece that is not built cannot be chec.rule: A piece that is not built cannot be checked against its drawn position; the K3 tolerance check should skip pieces with no built model.

a movable chair within 0.10 m of its dra.rule: A movable chair within 0.10 m of its drawn position is within tolerance; the K3 check should use a 0.10 m tolerance for chairs.

a dresser within 0.20 m of its drawn pos.rule: A dresser within 0.20 m of its drawn position is within tolerance; the K3 check should use a 0.20 m tolerance for large movable furniture.

a wardrobe within 0.10 m of its drawn po.rule: A wardrobe within 0.10 m of its drawn position is within tolerance; the K3 check should use a 0.10 m tolerance for large fixed-position furniture.

a floor lamp within 0.35 m of its drawn.rule: A floor lamp within 0.35 m of its drawn position is within tolerance; the K3 check should use a 0.35 m tolerance for small movable pieces.

an interior camera must be posed so that.rule: An interior camera must be posed so that no single door or wall element fills more than 40% of the frame; if a render check reports a door as indistinguishable from a wall, the camera is re-aimed to show the door in context.

downpipes on a facade must be rendered w.rule: Downpipes on a facade must be rendered with a material that integrates them into the wall surface; if a render check reports them as crude tubes, the facade material is changed to a smoother finish.

the entrance path must have a distinct m.rule: The entrance path must have a distinct material that defines it as a walkway; if a render check reports it as an untextured slab, the path material is changed to a paving look.

a room typed living must hold a seating.rule: A room typed living must hold a seating group (sofa + coffee table) to read as a living space; a sofa alone is a bare corner.

interior cameras must be placed at eye h.rule: Interior cameras must be placed at eye height (1.2-1.6 m) and at least 0.6 m from doors, showing the room's main fixtures.

a bathroom with a washing machine should.rule: A bathroom with a washing machine should have it placed in a utility zone or the room should be typed to reflect the mixed use.

a children's room should include a work.rule: A children's room should include a work group (desk + chair) to read as a functional child's room.

a bathroom set must include all standard.rule: A bathroom set must include all standard fixtures (bathtub, toilet, washbasin) without clashes.

a drawn label for a piece (e.g., dresser.rule: A drawn label for a piece (e.g., dresser) must be matched to a built piece within 1.0 m; if no place passes checks, the label is a false positive or the room layout is too constrained.

furniture pieces must not overlap; if a.rule: Furniture pieces must not overlap; if a clash is detected, the piece should be moved to the nearest free place.

furniture must not cover openings (windo.rule: Furniture must not cover openings (windows, doors); if a piece covers an opening, it should be moved to clear the opening.

elevations must have a view bearing or s.rule: Elevations must have a view bearing or side to be checked against the plans; if missing, the check is skipped and flagged.

drawn sections must align with the roof.rule: Drawn sections must align with the roof outline within 0.30 m; if not, the section is not checked point by point.
drawn sections must align with the roof.target: the drawn section r# is not checked point by point against the roof

elevations must have a view bearing or s.rule: Elevations must have a view bearing or side to be compared with the model; if missing, the comparison is skipped.

a dining group must fit within the room'.rule: A dining group must fit within the room's free spans; if no place passes checks, the group is not placed and the issue is flagged.

an entrance group must fit within the ro.rule: An entrance group must fit within the room's free spans; if no place passes checks, the group is not placed and the issue is flagged.

windows must have a library model that f.rule: Windows must have a library model that fits their size; if not, they are built parametrically in the style's finish.

kitchen fixtures must use a library mode.rule: Kitchen fixtures must use a library model that fits their size and style; if the parametric mesh is used, it is flagged as below library level.

the fitting stage must not fall back to.rule: The fitting stage must not fall back to a parametric mesh when a library model exists for the piece's type and size; a parametric build is only allowed when the catalogue has no model for that type at that size, and the run must log the missing model id so the gap can be filled.

the build stage must construct the balco.rule: The build stage must construct the balcony (sa_L1_balkon) with a railing and a finished floor when the documents label a BALKON outside the walls; a balcony door that opens onto an empty grey terrace is a missing site element, not a camera problem.

the build stage must not drop an opening.rule: The build stage must not drop an opening that the reading stage recorded with evidence; if an opening is read twice (as o_L1_001 was), the build stage must resolve the duplicate by keeping one instance and logging the merge, not by dropping both.

drawn cushions or pillows inside a sofa.rule: Drawn cushions or pillows inside a sofa or bed footprint are details of that piece's model, not separate furniture; the build stage should not create them as independent pieces.

structural grid bubbles (axis labels) ar.rule: Structural grid bubbles (axis labels) are drawing annotations and must not be built as 3D elements.

drawn columns supporting a veranda or ba.rule: Drawn columns supporting a veranda or balcony are built as posts of that structure, not as separate interior elements.

level mark symbols (kot) are drawing ann.rule: Level mark symbols (kot) are drawing annotations and must not be built as 3D elements.

labelled site areas (veranda, balcony) o.rule: Labelled site areas (veranda, balcony) outside the outer walls must be built as 3D structures with their own floor, railing, and support posts, even if no walls are drawn around them.

when two drawn outlines represent the sa.rule: When two drawn outlines represent the same piece (one inside the other), the build stage should merge them and build only one instance.

when a drawn outline is 60% or more insi.rule: When a drawn outline is 60% or more inside another piece of the same type, it is a duplicate or part of that piece and should not be built separately.

when a kitchen run is drawn as one outli.rule: When a kitchen run is drawn as one outline with its fixtures, the build stage should replace it with the individual counter segments and fixtures.

large outlines (3.89 x 1.65 m) that encl.rule: Large outlines (3.89 x 1.65 m) that enclose other pieces are rugs or zone outlines, not furniture; the decor rules handle rugs separately.

drawn cushions or pillows inside a sofa.rule: Drawn cushions or pillows inside a sofa footprint are details of that piece's model, not separate furniture; the build stage should not create them as independent pieces.

when a piece is marked 'not built' but h.rule: When a piece is marked 'not built' but has a valid library model available, the build stage should use that model to construct the piece.

when a cluster of drawn pieces is larger.rule: When a cluster of drawn pieces is larger than 4.5 m on a side, the build stage should recognize it as a group of furniture and build each piece individually, rather than treating it as a single untyped object.

drawn marks thinner than 0.2 m (e.g., ta.rule: Drawn marks thinner than 0.2 m (e.g., taps, valves, thresholds, shelf lines) are not furniture and should not be built as pieces.

when a section shows the ground floor at.rule: When a section shows the ground floor at a non-zero elevation (e.g., +0.50), the reading stage must offset all plan-level marks by that amount to align with the section's datum.

a labelled veranda, terrace or balcony i.rule: A labelled veranda, terrace or balcony in the documents must be built as a site platform with its own outline and, if drawn, a roof or pergola structure; it must not be left as 'no outline'.

a labelled outdoor area (veranda, balcon.rule: A labelled outdoor area (veranda, balcony, terrace) in the documents must be built as a platform with a floor and a railing, not dropped as 'no outline'.

a door on an upper floor that opens to t.rule: A door on an upper floor that opens to the outside must have a built balcony or landing to stand on; a door into the air is a build error.

a named piece in the documents (e.g. a d.rule: A named piece in the documents (e.g. a dresser) must be placed in the model; if it is missing, the room's program group for that piece must be built.

a door-to-door walkway of at least 0.60.rule: A door-to-door walkway of at least 0.60 m must be kept clear of furniture and fixtures; the layout solver must treat the door swing and the 0.60 m clearance path as hard constraints when placing pieces.

a bed's headboard must be flush against.rule: A bed's headboard must be flush against a wall; the layout solver must snap the headboard to the nearest wall within tolerance and refuse placements that leave it floating.

no furniture may block a door's swing or.rule: No furniture may block a door's swing or its 0.60 m clearance zone; the layout solver must treat door openings as no-go zones for piece placement.

no furniture may block a window's access.rule: No furniture may block a window's access or its 0.60 m clearance zone; the layout solver must treat window openings as no-go zones for piece placement.

a door-to-window walkway of at least 0.6.rule: A door-to-window walkway of at least 0.60 m must be kept clear of furniture and fixtures; the layout solver must treat the door swing and the 0.60 m clearance path as hard constraints when placing pieces.

every piece must be rendered with its fu.rule: Every piece must be rendered with its full geometry including legs and support structure; the render stage must verify that no piece appears to float above the floor.

every main fixture of a room (washbasin,.rule: Every main fixture of a room (washbasin, toilet, bathtub/shower) must be visible in at least one render of that room; the render stage must verify that all main fixtures are present in the frame.

a kitchen must have a complete functiona.rule: A kitchen must have a complete functional set: counter, hob/stove, sink, and upper cabinets; the layout stage must verify that all main kitchen pieces are present and visible.

every main fixture of a room (stove, fri.rule: Every main fixture of a room (stove, fridge, wall cabinets) must be visible in at least one render of that room; the render stage must verify that all main fixtures are present in the frame.

a living room must have a main seating a.rule: A living room must have a main seating anchor (sofa or sofa corner) and a dining set if the room is large enough; the layout stage must verify that the main seating group is present.
A living room must have a main seating anchor (sofa or sofa corner) and a coffee table; the layout stage must verify that the main living group is present.

every main fixture of a room (shower, to.rule: Every main fixture of a room (shower, toilet, washbasin) must be visible in at least one render of that room; the render stage must verify that all main fixtures are present in the frame.

f2/f3 must not clear a door when a bed (.rule: F2/F3 must not clear a door when a bed (or any tall piece) blocks its swing or the 0.60 m landing in front of it; a door is only 'fine' when its full swing arc and the landing are free of furniture.

e1 must reject any door whose threshold.rule: E1 must reject any door whose threshold is above 0.15 m above the floor of the room it opens into with no stair, step or ramp to reach it (a door into the air).

an interior camera must be posed so the.rule: An interior camera must be posed so the room's main furniture group is visible, not a bare wall or cabinet face; when a view is a flat surface, re-aim it at the room's main pieces.

a sanitary or bed model whose render sho.rule: A sanitary or bed model whose render shows a melted/low-poly blob must be swapped for a clean library model of the same footprint.

a bed model whose render shows a lumpy/l.rule: A bed model whose render shows a lumpy/low-poly mesh must be swapped for a clean library model of the same footprint.

a wardrobe model that clashes with the r.rule: A wardrobe model that clashes with the room's palette (glossy black on warm wood) must be swapped for a scandinavian/minimal model that matches.

a bed model whose render shows a crude l.rule: A bed model whose render shows a crude low-poly block must be swapped for a clean library model of the same footprint.

exterior trees must be high-quality mode.rule: Exterior trees must be high-quality models, not low-poly lollipop placeholders; when the site trees look like a video game, reduce their count or replace them with a better asset set.

scene check s2 failures on a level must.rule: Scene check S2 failures on a level must be resolved by re-running the build stage so the geometry is re-validated.

scene check s3 failures on a level must.rule: Scene check S3 failures on a level must be resolved by re-running the build stage so the geometry is re-validated.

the main walkway from the entrance door.rule: The main walkway from the entrance door must be at least 0.80 m clear between doors; when it is below that, move the blocking piece to the nearest free place.

a piece's front use zone must be reached.rule: A piece's front use zone must be reached by a 0.60 m walkway from the nearest door; when it is not, move the piece to the nearest free place that is.

a seating piece whose front use zone is.rule: A seating piece whose front use zone is not reached by a 0.60 m walkway from the room's door must be re-placed (or the room re-laid out) so the walkway reaches it; a clearance failure is a placement error, not a model error.

a drawn sanitary or kitchen fixture whos.rule: A drawn sanitary or kitchen fixture whose back is off its wall by more than 0.03 m must be re-snapped to the wall (or the room re-laid out) so its back rests on the wall; a small off-wall offset is a placement error, not a model error.

two kitchen counter modules that overlap.rule: Two kitchen counter modules that overlap must be re-placed as one run (re-layout of the room) so they do not collide; an overlap of drawn kitchen modules is a placement error.

a kitchen counter module that reaches th.rule: A kitchen counter module that reaches through the room outline (into a door or wall) must be re-placed (re-layout of the room) so it stays inside the room; a module crossing the outline is a placement error.

a kitchen counter whose front use zone i.rule: A kitchen counter whose front use zone is not reached by a 0.60 m walkway from the room's door must be re-placed (re-layout of the room) so the walkway reaches it; a clearance failure of a kitchen run is a placement error.

a drawn bathtub whose back is off its wa.rule: A drawn bathtub whose back is off its wall by more than 0.03 m must be re-snapped to the wall (or the room re-laid out) so its back rests on the wall; a small off-wall offset is a placement error, not a model error.

a drawn washbasin whose back is off its.rule: A drawn washbasin whose back is off its wall by more than 0.03 m must be re-snapped to the wall (or the room re-laid out) so its back rests on the wall; a small off-wall offset is a placement error, not a model error.

a piece whose free zone in front is bloc.rule: A piece whose free zone in front is blocked by another piece must be re-placed (or the room re-laid out) so the free zone is clear; a blocked front zone is a placement error.

the main walkway from the entrance door.rule: The main walkway from the entrance door must be at least 0.80 m wide between doors; if it is below 0.80 m, the pieces in the hall must be re-placed (re-layout) so the walkway is clear.
The main walkway from the entrance door must be at least 0.80 m wide between doors and windows; if it is below 0.80 m, the pieces in the hall must be re-placed (re-layout) so the walkway is clear.

a dresser whose back is off its wall by.rule: A dresser whose back is off its wall by more than 0.03 m must be re-placed (or the room re-laid out) so its back rests on the wall; a small off-wall offset is a placement error, not a model error.

a nightstand that overlaps a bed must be.rule: A nightstand that overlaps a bed must be re-placed (or the room re-laid out) so it does not collide; an overlap of a nightstand and a bed is a placement error.

a bed with less than 0.60 m free along i.rule: A bed with less than 0.60 m free along its side must be re-placed (or the room re-laid out) so at least 0.60 m is free; a clearance failure of a bed is a placement error.

a wardrobe whose front use zone is not r.rule: A wardrobe whose front use zone is not reached by a 0.60 m walkway from the room's door must be re-placed (or the room re-laid out) so the walkway reaches it; a clearance failure of a wardrobe is a placement error.

a shower that stands in front of a windo.rule: A shower that stands in front of a window (blocking it) must be re-placed (or the room re-laid out) so it does not block the window; a shower blocking a window is a placement error.

a sofa whose free zone in front is block.rule: A sofa whose free zone in front is blocked by another piece must be re-placed (or the room re-laid out) so the free zone is clear; a blocked front zone is a placement error.

a tall free-standing piece (lamp, plant).rule: A tall free-standing piece (lamp, plant) that the drawing places in front of a window is a layout choice, not a defect: the window is not blocked for use (sill 0.90 m, lamp 1.60 m beside it). Do not flag a floor lamp or potted plant standing in front of a window as a blocked opening; only flag pieces that physically prevent the window from being opened or used (a bed, a wardrobe, a radiator).

a fixture whose back is off a wall by le.rule: A fixture whose back is off a wall by less than 0.03 m (3 cm) is within the tolerance of a drawn layout and a library model's footprint; do not flag it as off-wall. Only flag offsets of 0.03 m or more.

a washbasin or toilet whose back is off.rule: A washbasin or toilet whose back is off a wall by less than 0.10 m (10 cm) is within the tolerance of a drawn layout; do not flag it as off-wall. Only flag offsets of 0.10 m or more, or cases where the fixture is clearly floating in the middle of the room.

a washing machine in a bathroom or utili.rule: A washing machine in a bathroom or utility room is a fixed appliance that is typically placed against a wall. Its 'front use zone' (the space needed to open the door) is not a walkway requirement in the same sense as a piece of furniture. Do not flag a washing machine's front zone as a walkway obstruction unless it physically blocks the door swing or the main circulation path of the room.

the exterior environment must include a.rule: The exterior environment must include a textured ground (grass, paving, or gravel), a reasonable number of trees (5-12), and a fence or hedge to define the plot boundary. A flat, untextured green plane with low-poly trees is a placeholder and must be replaced with a designed site.

every opening (window, door, or large op.rule: Every opening (window, door, or large opening) must have a visible frame or surround. A raw, unframed hole is a build error. If the opening is a large feature (e.g., a glass wall), it must have a frame or mullion that is visible in the render.

a piece of furniture (e.g., an armchair).rule: A piece of furniture (e.g., an armchair) must not be pushed flat against a wall under a window unless it is a console table or a bench. An armchair should be part of a seating arrangement, with space in front of it for use. If a room's layout has a piece of furniture in an awkward position, the room should be relaid out.

a piece that is planned to be built but.rule: A piece that is planned to be built but has no object in the scene is a build error. If the piece is a kitchen appliance (stove, fridge, sink), it must be built with a library model or a parametric family. If the current model is a 'module' (e.g., kitchen_run), it may not be visible or may be merged with the counter. Swap it for a standalone library model.

a drawn piece that is named in the docum.rule: A drawn piece that is named in the documents (e.g., 'SIFONIYER' for dresser) but is typed as 'unknown' or a different type in the model is a reading error. Retype the piece to the type named in the documents.

a piece named in the documents but not p.rule: A piece named in the documents but not present in the model is a reading error. If the piece is not built, add a camera view that shows the location where the piece should be, to highlight the missing piece.

a drawn piece that is a cluster larger t.rule: A drawn piece that is a cluster larger than 4.5 m on a side is not a single piece of furniture; it is a group of pieces or a built-in element. It should not be built as a single piece. Mark it as 'not furniture' with the kind 'other' and the evidence 'cluster larger than 4.5 m on a side: a group of drawn pieces'.

a room that has two labels (e.g., 'salon.rule: A room that has two labels (e.g., 'Salon' and 'YEMEK BÖLÜMÜ') is a combined living/dining room. The room type should be 'living' if the living area is larger, or 'dining' if the dining area is larger. If the room is a combined space, it should be typed as 'living' and the dining area should be considered part of the living room.

a stair that is not built at the upper l.rule: A stair that is not built at the upper level is a build error. The stair must be built at both levels (L0 and L1) to connect them. If the stair is not built at L1, fix its position to a valid spot within the room.

a cluster of strokes on the furniture la.rule: A cluster of strokes on the furniture layer that matches the footprint of a standard piece (e.g. 0.56 x 1.20 m for a sofa or chair) must be recognized as a piece, not left as unassigned strokes.

when a room outline contains two distinc.rule: When a room outline contains two distinct room labels (e.g. 'Mutfak' and 'ANTRE'), the reading stage must split the outline into two separate rooms based on the label anchors.

site areas explicitly labeled in the doc.rule: Site areas explicitly labeled in the documents (e.g. VERANDA, BALKON) must be built with their geometric outlines and appropriate materials/structures, not skipped.

if a piece is marked 'not built' but has.rule: If a piece is marked 'not built' but has a valid model available in the library, the build stage must assign that model and build the piece, rather than leaving it out.

if a piece is removed by an ai action bu.rule: If a piece is removed by an AI action but is still listed in the room's pieces, the furniture agent must either rebuild it or explicitly remove it from the room's piece list.

if a decor item's host is not built, the.rule: If a decor item's host is not built, the furniture agent must either build the host or reassign the decor to a built host.

site areas labeled in the documents (e.g.rule: Site areas labeled in the documents (e.g. VERANDA) must be built with their geometric outlines and structures, not left as 'NOT built (no outline)'.
Site areas labeled in the documents (e.g. BALKON) must be built with their geometric outlines and structures, not left as 'NOT built (no outline)'.

if a fixture's clearance is insufficient.rule: If a fixture's clearance is insufficient due to the room's size and the fixture's size, and the code has already tried to fix it, the finding is a layout constraint, not a misread.
If a fixture's clearance is insufficient due to the room's size and the fixture's position, and the code has already tried to fix it, the finding is a layout constraint, not a misread.
If a fixture's clearance is insufficient due to the room's size and the fixture's position, the finding is a layout constraint, not a misread.

if a piece is listed as a chair but is a.rule: If a piece is listed as a chair but is actually a fridge (based on its size and position in the kitchen), the reading stage must retype it as a fridge.

a drawn piece whose footprint is a singl.rule: A drawn piece whose footprint is a single square (width ≈ depth) and whose height is 1.4 m or more must be typed as a tall appliance (fridge, tall_cabinet) or a tall storage unit, never as a wall_cabinet; wall_cabinet is reserved for pieces whose depth is 0.45 m or less and whose height is 0.9 m or less, and it is always placed above a counter run, not standing on the floor.

a window's sightline must be kept clear.rule: A window's sightline must be kept clear of furniture; a piece that blocks the ray through an opening is moved or removed before the scene is accepted.

a kitchen counter is a low work surface;.rule: A kitchen counter is a low work surface; its top must be at working height (~0.90-0.95 m), never at 2.10 m, and it must sit fully inside the room, not in a door opening.

a balcony slab must be supported (column.rule: A balcony slab must be supported (columns or cantilever) and reached by a door from its room; a floating slab with a railing but no support or access is a build error.

a downpipe must connect to a gutter at t.rule: A downpipe must connect to a gutter at the top and end in a splash block at the bottom; a bare cylinder is a placeholder, not a finished rain-water detail.

the main entrance must be legible: a cle.rule: The main entrance must be legible: a clear door leaf, handle, canopy or step detail, and an unambiguous porch/landing so a client can see where the front door is and how it is reached.

every from_documents window in a room mu.rule: Every from_documents window in a room must be visible in at least one of the room's required camera views; if no free camera point can show the room's key pieces and the window, the room layout must be changed, not the camera.

every from_documents door in a room must.rule: Every from_documents door in a room must be visible in at least one of the room's required camera views; if no free camera point can show the room's key pieces and the door, the room layout must be changed, not the camera.

a washbasin must be at a usable working.rule: A washbasin must be at a usable working height (rim ~0.85 m) and reachable; a basin wedged behind a toilet at a low height is a build error.

a bathroom door must not open directly i.rule: A bathroom door must not open directly into the basin/toilet cluster; the approach to the fixtures must be clear of the door swing.

a stair opening and landing edge must ha.rule: A stair opening and landing edge must have a proper guard (balustrade or full-height glass) with no large open gap; a thin placeholder glass panel is a fall risk and a build error.

the entrance area must have finished ste.rule: The entrance area must have finished steps, handrails, and a finished terrace slab; raw, untextured, floating geometry is a build error.

a door must be rendered as a door (leaf,.rule: A door must be rendered as a door (leaf, frame, handle), not as a different object (e.g. wall art); a door that looks like something else in a camera view is a build error.

a drawn piece must match its drawn size.rule: A drawn piece must match its drawn size and position within tolerance (0.05 m); a model that differs in size or place is a build error.

a drawn desk that the code retyped from.rule: A drawn desk that the code retyped from its size and room (adjusted_by_ai) is locked to that type; a 0.15 m offset from its drawn place is a fit error the furniture agent must resolve by re-fitting the piece, not by retyping it.

an interior camera that frames a door so.rule: An interior camera that frames a door so closely it reads as a wall panel must be moved to a free point that shows the door in context with the room's main furniture.

an interior camera in a hall that frames.rule: An interior camera in a hall that frames a door so closely it fills the frame must be moved to a free point that shows the door in context with the hall's other elements.

a drawn piece 0.21 x 0.20 m in a living.rule: A drawn piece 0.21 x 0.20 m in a living room that the AI could not type (potted_plant, unknown) and that is not built should be marked as not furniture if it is a symbol or mark, not a real piece.

a drawn cluster larger than 4.5 m on a s.rule: A drawn cluster larger than 4.5 m on a side that is not built and has no type should be marked as not furniture if it is a group of symbols or marks, not real furniture.

a drawn piece 1.20 x 0.55 m in a bedroom.rule: A drawn piece 1.20 x 0.55 m in a bedroom that the documents name as a dresser ('*SIFONIYER') should be retyped as a dresser, not left untyped.

a dresser named by the documents at a lo.rule: A dresser named by the documents at a location where no drawn dresser stands should be added by the furniture agent if the nearest valid place is within 1.5 m of the text.

a dressing room (soyunma odası) that is.rule: A dressing room (Soyunma Odası) that is typed 'other' and holds only a wardrobe should be typed as a bedroom/dressing room and furnished as a set.

a small drawn piece around a level mark.rule: A small drawn piece around a level mark text (e.g. '+0,50') that was read as furniture should be marked as a level mark, not furniture.

when the section prints the ground floor.rule: When the section prints the ground floor at a non-zero level (e.g. +0.50), the plans must be read with that offset so that all relative marks are correct.

a washing machine named by the documents.rule: A washing machine named by the documents in a bathroom should be verified by the furniture agent for correct placement and build status.

a dresser named by the documents in a be.rule: A dresser named by the documents in a bedroom should be verified by the furniture agent for correct placement and build status.
A dresser named by the documents in a bedroom that is not listed in the room's pieces should be added and placed by the furniture agent.

a 2.15 m sliding door read from its line.rule: A 2.15 m sliding door read from its lines (no swing arc) in the outer wall of a room, with a drawn piece standing across its approach, should be read as a window, not a door.

a 1.10 m gap in the outer wall of a room.rule: A 1.10 m gap in the outer wall of a room, with drawn pieces standing across its approach, should be read as a window, not a door.

an outer-wall gap that is fully or nearl.rule: An outer-wall gap that is fully or nearly blocked by a drawn fixed run (kitchen counter, bath wall) and has no outside access is a window at the floor's sill, not a door; the reading must classify it by what is on its approach, not by its width.

a bathroom set (bathtub, washbasin, toil.rule: A bathroom set (bathtub, washbasin, toilet) must be solved as one unit so the pieces do not overlap; single-piece fixes that leave a real overlap are not a solution.

a dressing room's wardrobe and its partn.rule: A dressing room's wardrobe and its partners must be solved as one unit so the pieces do not overlap; single-piece fixes that leave a real overlap are not a solution.

a built piece must not cover a window op.rule: A built piece must not cover a window opening; the furniture agent must re-place the piece to clear the opening.

the big loop must run enough fix cycles.rule: The big loop must run enough fix cycles to raise the house score; stopping at the deadline with 303 open major points means the time budget was not used for more cycles.

a drawn piece whose type the room does n.rule: A drawn piece whose type the room does not allow must be retyped to a type that fits its size and its room, not kept unverified.

a dressing room smaller than the minimum.rule: A dressing room smaller than the minimum footprint of its dressing group (wardrobe + mirror + bench) must be flagged as too small for the group, and the group must be dropped or the room enlarged, not left with nothing placed.

a small drawn piece centred on a level-m.rule: A small drawn piece centred on a level-mark text (e.g. '+0,50') is a level-mark symbol, not furniture: mark it not_furniture with kind level_mark.

views flagged for review must be re-pose.rule: Views flagged for review must be re-posed or removed in the next agent round before the run is accepted.

when a tall storage piece (wardrobe) is.rule: When a tall storage piece (wardrobe) is drawn against a wall that also carries a window/door and no free wall span exists within the move limit, the fit stage must flag the drawing conflict for the architect (move the window or the piece) instead of letting the agent retry moves that the geometry forbids.

a kitchen room whose drawn run lacks a h.rule: A kitchen room whose drawn run lacks a hob/stove or a fridge must be completed by the group solver (place_group kitchen_run) before the agent is asked to relayout; the agent must not be asked to relayout a room whose program is incomplete.

a floor lamp whose generated model has a.rule: A floor lamp whose generated model has a shade at head height (blocking the view) must be swapped to a library model whose shade top is below 1.50 m; the fit stage must reject generated floor-lamp models whose shade exceeds 1.50 m.

a washbasin drawn within 0.50 m of a win.rule: A washbasin drawn within 0.50 m of a window/door that it blocks must be moved by the fit stage to the nearest free wall span; if no free span exists within 0.50 m, the drawing conflict is flagged for the architect.

a living room larger than 30 m2 must hav.rule: A living room larger than 30 m2 must have its seating and dining groups placed by the group solver before the agent is asked to relayout; the agent must not be asked to relayout a room whose program groups are missing.

a shoe cabinet under a sloped ceiling mu.rule: A shoe cabinet under a sloped ceiling must be swapped to a library model whose height is at most 2.80 m and whose style matches the project; the fit stage must reject models that fail the sloped-ceiling height cap.

the architect's rule f5 must explicitly.rule: The architect's rule F5 must explicitly list the cases where F9 (overlap) is acceptable (e.g. kitchen counters that share a wall) or the critic must not flag them.

the architect's rule s4 must explicitly.rule: The architect's rule S4 must explicitly list the cases where G10 (clear in front) is acceptable (e.g. bathtub in a small bathroom) or the critic must not flag them.

the architect's rule f4 must explicitly.rule: The architect's rule F4 must explicitly list the cases where F6 (free zone blocked) is acceptable (e.g. armchair in a corner) or the critic must not flag them.

the architect's rule f3 must explicitly.rule: The architect's rule F3 must explicitly list the cases where G12 (piece in front of window) is acceptable (e.g. wardrobe under a high window) or the critic must not flag them.

an interior view of a small room (under.rule: An interior view of a small room (under 6 m2) must be posed to show the room's main furniture; if no free pose exists, the view is removed.

exterior views must not use low-poly lol.rule: Exterior views must not use low-poly lollipop trees; if no high-quality tree model is available, the site trees are set to 0.

interior views looking out a window must.rule: Interior views looking out a window must not use a flat, low-poly cartoon landscape; if no high-quality backdrop is available, the site trees are set to 0 and the ground is set to a neutral look.

a kitchen counter that cuts a wall by mo.rule: A kitchen counter that cuts a wall by more than 0.030 m must be moved by the fit stage to the nearest valid spot; if no valid spot exists within 0.50 m, the drawing conflict is flagged for the architect.

the exterior landscape must use the site.rule: The exterior landscape must use the site's real tree models, not the low-poly placeholder stand-in, so that views through windows read as a real garden.

a washbasin model must carry its own fau.rule: A washbasin model must carry its own faucet and mirror-ready top; a bare basin shell is a placeholder, not a finished fixture.

a bathtub model must include its fitting.rule: A bathtub model must include its fittings (faucet, shower head) in the asset; a bare tub shell is a placeholder.

sanitary ware must match the room's stat.rule: Sanitary ware must match the room's stated style; a dated two-piece model in a modern tiled bathroom is a mismatch.

a kitchen run must be built as a designe.rule: A kitchen run must be built as a designed run with handles, material variation and appliance integration, not as a row of blank parametric boxes.

a seating group must not be four identic.rule: A seating group must not be four identical chairs; the set needs variety in form and colour to read as designed.

a dining table must match the room's pal.rule: A dining table must match the room's palette and the seating set; a plain boxy slab is a placeholder.

a coffee table must match the room's pal.rule: A coffee table must match the room's palette; a third clashing wood tone is a mismatch.

chairs at one table must be the same mod.rule: Chairs at one table must be the same model; mixing two models reads as a mismatched set.

armchairs placed side by side must form.rule: Armchairs placed side by side must form a set; different models, colours and styles are a mismatch.

a bathroom must be styled with its full.rule: A bathroom must be styled with its full set (mirror, towel, soap, hardware); a bare washbasin is a placeholder.

a dresser model must have drawer lines,.rule: A dresser model must have drawer lines, texture and a top surface; a plain white box with floating dots is a placeholder.

a nightstand model must match the room's.rule: A nightstand model must match the room's wood tone and finish; a plain box in a clashing warm wood is a wrong model, not a placement problem.

an interior camera must frame the room's.rule: An interior camera must frame the room's main functional group, not a blank corner or a single fixture up close.

the exterior site must use realistic tre.rule: The exterior site must use realistic tree models and a textured ground plane, not low-poly placeholder 'lollipop' trees on a flat green plane.

sanitary fixtures must use styled, moder.rule: Sanitary fixtures must use styled, modern models that match the room's design aesthetic, not generic 'hospital' or 'construction site' models.

a washbasin must be a styled, modern mod.rule: A washbasin must be a styled, modern model that matches the room's aesthetic, not a plain utility sink with exposed chrome pipes.

an office chair in a bedroom must be a s.rule: An office chair in a bedroom must be a styled model that matches the room's soft, light-wood aesthetic, not a generic black utilitarian model.

a desk in a bedroom must be a styled mod.rule: A desk in a bedroom must be a styled model that matches the room's quality and aesthetic, not a plain, thin-topped placeholder.

a double bed must have a nightstand on b.rule: A double bed must have a nightstand on both sides; if the schedule lists two, both must be present and symmetric.

paired armchairs must be the same model.rule: Paired armchairs must be the same model or a coherent set; mismatched styles (white molded shell vs. grey upholstered wing) look like a random selection.

a floor lamp must have correct scale and.rule: A floor lamp must have correct scale and proportion; a shade that is too large and sits at head height, blocking a window, is a wrong model.

a hall/entrance must have an entrance gr.rule: A hall/entrance must have an entrance group (shoe cabinet, console, lighting) to look like a designed entrance, not a bare shell.

a stair and its railing must use a model.rule: A stair and its railing must use a model that expresses the project's style, not a plain, generic system that looks like a default placeholder.

an interior camera must frame the room's.rule: An interior camera must frame the room's main pieces and layout, not be too close to a corner and cut off the main furniture.

doors must be built with a frame, a hand.rule: Doors must be built with a frame, a handle and a leaf texture that matches the project's door material slot; a bare flat slab is a placeholder and must be rejected at the render check.

the main entrance door must be built wit.rule: The main entrance door must be built with a frame, handle and leaf texture matching the project style; a generic flat white slab is a placeholder.

a living room's seating group must be so.rule: A living room's seating group must be solved as one set (sofas, coffee table, rug) anchored on the drawn sofa, not as independent pieces placed by the fitter.

the exterior visible through windows mus.rule: The exterior visible through windows must use the site's real trees and ground, not a placeholder low-poly landscape.

a bathroom's set (bathtub, toilet, washb.rule: A bathroom's set (bathtub, toilet, washbasin) must be solved as one group so no member is missing or crammed into a corner.

a toilet model must match the style of t.rule: A toilet model must match the style of the bathroom's other fixtures (bathtub, tiles) to form a coherent set.

a bedroom's work group (desk, office cha.rule: A bedroom's work group (desk, office chair) must be solved as one set matching the room's style, not as independent generic pieces.

a bedroom's chest group (dresser, wardro.rule: A bedroom's chest group (dresser, wardrobe) must be solved as one set matching the room's style and scale, not as independent oversized pieces.

a bedroom's sleeping group (bed, nightst.rule: A bedroom's sleeping group (bed, nightstands) must be solved as one set with matching models and scales, not as independent mismatched pieces.

an interior camera must show the room's.rule: An interior camera must show the room's main fixtures, not be pressed against a wall or glass panel.

a door or window leaf that renders as a.rule: A door or window leaf that renders as a flat, untextured slab is a material-slot failure: the door and window_frame slots must carry a real finish (wood, painted or metal) from the style, never the default grey.

an interior camera that frames an open s.rule: An interior camera that frames an open stairwell edge or a floating landing reads as a safety/logic failure; the hall view must be posed to show the hall's furniture and doors, not the unguarded stair opening.

a small hall/corridor view aimed at a co.rule: A small hall/corridor view aimed at a corner and a door leaf reads as an empty, unstyled space; the camera must be posed to show the room's anchor (its furniture) and the door, not a bare wall.

a bedroom render that shows a sofa and n.rule: A bedroom render that shows a sofa and no bed is a furniture-placement failure: the room's bed must be the anchor the camera shows, and a sofa is not a substitute for the sleeping group.

a view dominated by a blank wall and a d.rule: A view dominated by a blank wall and a door leaf is unbalanced; the camera must be posed to show the room's furniture, with the door as context, not the subject.

a dressing-room camera pressed against t.rule: A dressing-room camera pressed against the wardrobe shows a wall and door leaf instead of the room; the view must be posed from a free point to show the room's door and its storage.

a decor cushion that penetrates its host.rule: A decor cushion that penetrates its host by more than 0.03 m is not rested and is dropped; the seating agent must re-seat it on the host's top surface.

a sideboard or console pushed into a cor.rule: A sideboard or console pushed into a corner with a large empty wall beside it is an unbalanced composition; the storage agent must re-place it along a wall span that balances the room.

an armchair pushed flat against a wall u.rule: An armchair pushed flat against a wall under a window instead of being part of the seating arrangement looks staged; the seating agent must pull it into the group.

a washbasin that reads as a floating sla.rule: A washbasin that reads as a floating slab with an unclear wall/counter relationship is a fixture-anchoring failure; the bathroom agent must re-anchor it to the wall or counter at working height.

a ground that renders as a flat, untextu.rule: A ground that renders as a flat, untextured green plane is a material-slot failure: the ground slot must carry a real ground look (grass, paving, gravel), never the default viewport floor.

exterior backdrop quality (flat ground,.rule: Exterior backdrop quality (flat ground, lollipop trees, low-detail sky) is a global render/scene setting, not a per-opening geometry defect; do not file it against a specific window or opening.

the exterior scene must use a textured g.rule: The exterior scene must use a textured ground and a realistic tree count (not lollipop placeholders) so the site reads as a believable landscape, not a flat backdrop.

a fridge (or any appliance) must use a l.rule: A fridge (or any appliance) must use a library model with sufficient mesh detail (>= 3000 triangles); a crude low-poly box is a placeholder and must be swapped for a detailed model of the same footprint.

a lone or unstyled cushion is a decor/st.rule: A lone or unstyled cushion is a decor/styling preference, not a geometry defect of the host sofa; do not file it against the sofa piece.

in a large living room, the dining group.rule: In a large living room, the dining group must be placed in a usable position (not shoved against a glazed wall with awkward chair angles) so the open floor is used sensibly.

a flat, low-quality view outside a windo.rule: A flat, low-quality view outside a window is a global exterior/backdrop render setting, not a per-opening defect; fix it once via the exterior scene, not per window.

a drawn piece that an ai pass names with.rule: A drawn piece that an AI pass names with a type fitting its size and room must be typed and built, not discarded as a 'detail' of a neighbouring piece.

the reading stage must read attdef (attr.rule: The reading stage must read ATTDEF (attribute definition) entities in DWG files and pass their text values to the ledger, so that attribute-driven labels (room names, areas, notes) are not silently dropped.

site decor symbols read on an upper leve.rule: Site decor symbols read on an upper level that duplicate the ground plan's symbols at the same location are not separate site elements and need not be used; only unique L0 site decor is required.

when a room outline holds two distinct l.rule: When a room outline holds two distinct labels (e.g. a living room and a named dining zone), the reading stage must split the outline into separate rooms so each labelled space is its own room in the model.

the reading stage must capture printed a.rule: The reading stage must capture printed area labels (e.g. '9,00 m2') for each named space and pass them to the ledger so the area check can compare the drawn area against the modelled area.

when the reading stage chooses a wall la.rule: When the reading stage chooses a wall layer by evidence (closure rate, stroke pairing) and documents the runner-up and the primitives left out, the choice is valid and the left-out primitives are not a lost-element finding.

site decor symbols read on an upper leve.rule: Site decor symbols read on an upper level that duplicate the ground plan's symbols at the same location are not separate site elements and need not be used.

the reading stage must account for every.rule: The reading stage must account for every named layer in the DWG: if a layer's name indicates a fixture (e.g. 'DENIZLIK' = bathtub) and its geometry is not used by the model, the ledger must flag it so the fixture's drawn outline is checked against the built piece.

when a reading records the same opening.rule: When a reading records the same opening twice (duplicate evidence) and the build stage cannot resolve the duplicate, the build must keep the opening at its drawn position and flag the duplicate for review; it must not drop the opening from the model.

when a room outline holds the labels of.rule: When a room outline holds the labels of two rooms, the reading stage must split the outline into two rooms at the wall that separates them, rather than keeping the largest label and discarding the other.

when a bed_double is placed under a slop.rule: When a bed_double is placed under a sloped ceiling and the render check sees it as a bed_single, the fit stage must verify that the bed's height and the ceiling clearance are consistent with a double bed, and if not, adjust the bed model or the ceiling height.

when a drawn piece is more than 0.3 m fr.rule: When a drawn piece is more than 0.3 m from its drawn place and the move is refused by the drawn_lock rule, the layout stage must check whether the piece's drawn position is valid (not in a wall, not blocking a door) and if so, allow the move; if the drawn position is invalid, the reading stage must correct the drawn position.

a room of 3.1 m2 with a single shoe cabi.rule: A room of 3.1 m2 with a single shoe cabinet and no other furniture is a storage/utility space, not a hall; the reading should type it storage.

elevation-to-plan opening checks must be.rule: Elevation-to-plan opening checks must be skipped (not flagged as a failed check) when the elevation has no north arrow or view bearing to orient it against the plan.

a drawn section is only checked point-by.rule: A drawn section is only checked point-by-point against the roof when its ends align with the roof outline within 0.30 m; otherwise the check is skipped and the section is left for manual review.
a drawn section is only checked point-by.target: the drawn section r# is not checked point by point against the roof

elevation-to-model comparison is skipped.rule: Elevation-to-model comparison is skipped for any elevation that has neither a view bearing nor a side, and is not reported as a failed check.

when a dining group has no candidate pos.rule: When a dining group has no candidate position that fits the room's free spans, the solver must stop after the first refusal and leave the group for review instead of retrying the same span.

when an entrance group has no candidate.rule: When an entrance group has no candidate position that fits the room's free spans, the solver must stop after the first refusal and leave the group for review instead of retrying other spans.

when no library model of the building's.rule: When no library model of the building's window family fits an opening's size, the opening is built parametric in the style's finish and the finding is closed as a known library gap, not a defect.

a sink_kitchen built as a parametric mes.rule: A sink_kitchen built as a parametric mesh should be swapped to a library model of the same type when one fits the piece's size and the room's style.

a wall_cabinet built as a parametric mes.rule: A wall_cabinet built as a parametric mesh is a known library gap when no library model of the same type fits the piece's size; the finding is closed as a gap, not a defect.

a wardrobe whose model looks plain and i.rule: A wardrobe whose model looks plain and institutional should be swapped to a library model of the same type that matches the project's scandinavian/modern style.

a shoe_cabinet whose model looks plain a.rule: A shoe_cabinet whose model looks plain and boxy should be swapped to a library model of the same type that matches the project's minimal/modern style.

a door whose model looks plain and gener.rule: A door whose model looks plain and generic is a known library gap when no library model of the same type and style is available; the finding is closed as a gap, not a defect.

flat, untextured white wall surfaces tha.rule: Flat, untextured white wall surfaces that read as bare material should be given a textured plaster look to avoid a cheap, institutional appearance.

a stone path that looks like a rough, un.rule: A stone path that looks like a rough, untextured placeholder should be given a paving_stone look to read as a finished surface.

an office_chair whose model looks unfini.rule: An office_chair whose model looks unfinished and out of step with the room's lighter oak should be swapped to a library model of the same type that matches the room's style.

when a door opens onto a site area (balc.rule: When a door opens onto a site area (balcony, veranda) that the build stage left unbuilt (no outline), the render shows a bare default terrace; the fix is to build the site area's outline and railing, not to restyle the door.

interior doors of one house should share.rule: Interior doors of one house should share a single door material look so they read as a matched set; a generic mixed wood tone breaks the set.

a plain flat wood slab door clashes with.rule: A plain flat wood slab door clashes with a modern glass-and-metal interior; the door material should match the house's finish palette.

windows must render with a visible frame.rule: Windows must render with a visible frame and glazing (not a black void); the window_frame material must be a real frame look, not a dark void.

opaque dark windows make the house feel.rule: Opaque dark windows make the house feel cold; the window frame/glazing material should allow interior light to read.

an opening read twice and merged into on.rule: An opening read twice and merged into one is not a loss; the conservation check should not flag a deduplicated opening that remains in the final list.

drawing annotations (axis bubbles, grid.rule: Drawing annotations (axis bubbles, grid labels, level marks) are not building elements and should not be flagged as lost when not built.
