cushions/pillows drawn on a host piece a.rule: Cushions/pillows drawn on a host piece are details of that piece, not separate furniture; they should not be flagged as lost.

cushions/pillows that are part of a libr.rule: Cushions/pillows that are part of a library model are not separate drawn pieces; they should not be flagged as lost.

axis labels are drawing annotations, not.rule: Axis labels are drawing annotations, not building elements; not building them is correct.

columns that are built as part of a site.rule: Columns that are built as part of a site structure (veranda posts) are not lost; the conservation check should credit them to the structure.

level marks are drawing annotations, not.rule: Level marks are drawing annotations, not building elements; not building them is correct.

exterior area labels are text annotation.rule: Exterior area labels are text annotations; their surfaces are built from site materials, so the label itself is not a lost element.

a kitchen counter read twice and built o.rule: A kitchen counter read twice and built once is a correct deduplication, not a loss.

a piece drawn inside another piece (high.rule: A piece drawn inside another piece (high overlap) is a duplicate or part, not a separate element to build.

a kitchen run drawn as one outline is co.rule: A kitchen run drawn as one outline is correctly decomposed into its counter segments and fixtures; the outline itself is not a lost element.

a drawn outline that encloses a group of.rule: A drawn outline that encloses a group of pieces and has no thickness of its own is a rug or zone boundary, not a furniture piece; it is not built as a piece.

a small drawn mark (under 0.30 m on a si.rule: A small drawn mark (under 0.30 m on a side) that lies inside a larger piece's footprint is a detail of that piece (cushion, pillow, seam), not a separate piece.

a piece removed by the ai's remove_piece.rule: A piece removed by the AI's remove_piece action is a deliberate design decision; it is not a lost element unless the documents show it is required.

a drawn cluster larger than 4.5 m on a s.rule: A drawn cluster larger than 4.5 m on a side in a bedroom or living room is a built-in or long furniture run (desk, window seat, storage); it should be split into its constituent pieces or built as a custom run, not discarded as a group.

a drawn mark thinner than 0.20 m on a si.rule: A drawn mark thinner than 0.20 m on a side that fits no furniture type is a detail (tap, valve, threshold, shelf line), not a piece.

a small drawn mark (under 0.50 m on a si.rule: A small drawn mark (under 0.50 m on a side) that lies inside a larger piece's footprint (60% or more) is a detail of that piece, not a separate piece.

a nightstand that cannot be placed withi.rule: A nightstand that cannot be placed within 1.0 m of the bed after a bed resize should be re-placed in the next furniture round, not discarded.

the upper end of a stair that arrives fr.rule: The upper end of a stair that arrives from a lower level is not built again on the upper level if there is no level above; it is a single stair element spanning both levels.

a decor item that rests on a host piece.rule: A decor item that rests on a host piece is not built if the host is not built; it is a consequence of the host's removal, not a separate loss.
A decor item that rests on a host piece is not built if the host is not built; it is a consequence of the host's non-construction, not a separate loss.

a door symbol on a symbol layer that dup.rule: A door symbol on a symbol layer that duplicates an already-built door is a redundant symbol, not a lost element; do not flag it as a conservation loss.

hatch entities on a tarama/hatch layer a.rule: Hatch entities on a TARAMA/hatch layer are drawing annotations, not buildable elements; they are never a conservation loss when not built.

a drawn outdoor-space edge or step that.rule: A drawn outdoor-space edge or step that is already carried by a built veranda/balcony element is not a loss; the annotation is satisfied by the built element.

anchor the building frame to the drawn o.rule: Anchor the building frame to the drawn outer wall faces, not to the sheet outline corner; when the outer wall does not start at the sheet corner, apply the offset so all region and sheet coordinates are read relative to the true outer wall.

when a section prints the ground floor a.rule: When a section prints the ground floor at a non-zero datum (e.g. +0.50), read all plan relative marks against the building's true ground level (z 0), not the section's printed datum, so heights are not shifted by the datum offset.

a small drawn piece surrounding a level-.rule: A small drawn piece surrounding a level-mark text is a level-mark symbol, not furniture; it is correctly moved to symbols and not built.

when a document names a fixture in a roo.rule: When a document names a fixture in a room and the room's program already includes that fixture type, the furniture agent must place and verify it at the named location in its next round rather than leaving it unverified.

when a document names a dresser in a bed.rule: When a document names a dresser in a bedroom and the room's program includes a dresser, the furniture agent must place and verify it at the named location in its next round.

When a document names a dresser in a bedroom, the furniture agent must add and place a dresser in that room at or near the named location in its next round, even if the room's current piece list omits it.

when a document marks a dining zone in a.rule: When a document marks a dining zone in a living room and the room's program includes a table_dining, the furniture agent must place and verify the dining set at the marked zone in its next round, resolving any walkway conflicts.

a small seat drawn adjacent to and facin.rule: A small seat drawn adjacent to and facing a dining table is correctly typed as a chair by context; no retype is needed.

when a document names a dresser in a bed.rule: When a document names a dresser in a bedroom and no drawn dresser is at the named location, the furniture agent must add a dresser to that room in its next round, placing it at the nearest valid spot to the named location.

a warning that an opening is 'no passage.rule: A warning that an opening is 'no passage' because furniture stands across its approach is a false alarm when the opening is read as a window (sill >= 0.90 m); only true doors (sill at floor) need a clear approach.

a hall or corridor with an area below 3.rule: A hall or corridor with an area below 3 m2 is expected to have no furniture; a warning about missing furniture in such a room is a false alarm.

when two fixtures in a bathroom overlap,.rule: When two fixtures in a bathroom overlap, the smaller or more flexible fixture (e.g. washbasin) should be moved to a free spot, not the larger fixed one (e.g. bathtub).

furniture should not block the view or a.rule: Furniture should not block the view or access to a window; if a piece covers a window, it should be moved to a free spot.

a labelled veranda, terrace, or balcony.rule: A labelled veranda, terrace, or balcony in the documents must be built as a site area with a floor, and if columns or a roof are drawn, they must be included in the model.

a labelled veranda, terrace or balcony i.rule: A labelled veranda, terrace or balcony in the documents must be built as a site platform with its own outline, floor and railing, not dropped as 'no outline'.

an exterior door on an upper floor must.rule: An exterior door on an upper floor must have a built access (balcony, terrace, or external stair) that reaches its threshold.

a piece that overlaps another piece in t.rule: A piece that overlaps another piece in the same room is a fit failure: the layout stage must re-place it (or the room) so no two pieces intersect, before the render.

a kitchen room must be furnished as a co.rule: A kitchen room must be furnished as a complete run: the counter, the cooking zone (stove/hob) and the upper storage (wall cabinets) are one set; if the run is missing its cooking or storage members, the fit stage must complete the group rather than leave a bare counter.

a bedroom's secondary work group (desk,.rule: A bedroom's secondary work group (desk, office chair, and its supporting pieces) is part of the room's program; if the desk is listed but not built, the fit stage must place the work group rather than leave the room an empty shell.

a hall/entrance room's program includes.rule: A hall/entrance room's program includes its storage (shoe cabinet); if the listed piece is not built, the fit stage must place the entrance group rather than leave the corridor empty.

the exterior context seen through window.rule: The exterior context seen through windows must be a believable site (ground material, sky, and real trees), not a low-poly placeholder; the site stage must build the landscape to a renderable standard.

a living room's seating group must be a.rule: A living room's seating group must be a coherent set: matching sofas and a coffee table between them; if two mismatched sofas face each other with no table, the fit stage must re-solve the seating group as one unit.

an interior camera must frame the room's.rule: An interior camera must frame the room's main group at eye height, not a bare wall or door leaf; if the camera is aimed down a corridor and the room's furniture is out of frame, the camera stage must re-aim it to show the room's pieces.

An interior camera must frame the room's main group at eye height, not a flat wall or wardrobe face; if the camera is pressed against a surface, the camera stage must re-aim it to show the room's pieces.

a scene check failure (s2) on a level in.rule: A scene check failure (S2) on a level indicates a geometry or placement error in the build stage; the build stage must be re-run to resolve the failed check.

a scene check failure (s3) on a level in.rule: A scene check failure (S3) on a level indicates a geometry or placement error in the build stage; the build stage must be re-run to resolve the failed check.

a kitchen counter must be against a wall.rule: A kitchen counter must be against a wall or integrated into the main run, not a freestanding block in the middle of the room; the fit stage must place the counter as part of the kitchen run.

a large living room (55.6 m2) must be fu.rule: A large living room (55.6 m2) must be furnished with its full program (seating, coffee table, storage, decor); if the room reads as barren, the fit stage must place the missing groups.

an interior camera must frame the room's.rule: An interior camera must frame the room's main group at eye height, not a bare untextured surface; if the frame is filled by a flat placeholder wall, the camera stage must re-aim it.

the exterior context must be a believabl.rule: The exterior context must be a believable site with ground material, sky, and landscape, not a flat untextured white void; the site stage must build the exterior to a renderable standard.

when a furniture-layer cluster in a bedr.rule: When a furniture-layer cluster in a bedroom is larger than 4.5 m on a side, the reading must split it into its individual drawn pieces (sofa, chairs, table) rather than leaving the strokes unassigned; a cluster that big is a group, not a single piece.

site areas labelled in the documents (ve.rule: Site areas labelled in the documents (VERANDA, BALKON) must be built as outlined structures (slab, railing, roof where drawn) from their site.paving/grass surfaces, not left as 'no outline'; a labelled site area is part of the building envelope.

a drawn cluster larger than 4.5 m on a s.rule: A drawn cluster larger than 4.5 m on a side must be broken down into its individual pieces (by the reading or the build) and each piece built; a cluster is never left as a single untyped 'not built' element.

a site area labelled veranda in the docu.rule: A site area labelled VERANDA in the documents must be built as an outlined structure (slab, railing, roof where drawn) with its paving and furniture; it is not optional site decoration.

a site area labelled balkon in the docum.rule: A site area labelled BALKON in the documents must be built as an outlined structure (slab, railing, roof where drawn) on its level; it is not optional site decoration.

a bathroom render must frame the toilet;.rule: A bathroom render must frame the toilet; a missing main piece in the frame is a camera miss, not a missing piece, when the piece is listed in the room.

a kitchen render must frame the dining s.rule: A kitchen render must frame the dining set; a missing main piece in the frame is a camera miss, not a missing piece, when the piece is listed in the room.

a kitchen render must frame the upper ca.rule: A kitchen render must frame the upper cabinets; a missing main piece in the frame is a camera miss, not a missing piece, when the piece is listed in the room.

a living room render must frame the dini.rule: A living room render must frame the dining set; a missing main piece in the frame is a camera miss, not a missing piece, when the piece is listed in the room.

a piece listed in a room's program that.rule: A piece listed in a room's program that is marked 'not built' must be built (fitted and placed) before the run ends; a 'not built' flag on a program piece is a build failure, not a camera miss.

a dressing room render must frame the wa.rule: A dressing room render must frame the wardrobes; a missing main piece in the frame is a camera miss, not a missing piece, when the piece is listed in the room.

a bathroom set (bathtub, washbasin, toil.rule: A bathroom set (bathtub, washbasin, toilet) must be placed with no overlaps; the solver must find a non-overlapping layout or the run must flag it as unresolved.

a window's sightline (ray through the op.rule: A window's sightline (ray through the opening) must not be blocked by furniture; the solver must place furniture clear of window sightlines.

a kitchen counter's top must be at its w.rule: A kitchen counter's top must be at its working height (0.90-0.97 m); a counter built at 2.10 m is a misread size or a wrong model, and the build stage must reject or correct it.

an entrance area with stairs must have a.rule: An entrance area with stairs must have a clear, coherent layout: the main door, side door, steps, and handrail must form a legible sequence; the build stage must verify this coherence.

a door to a balcony or external landing.rule: A door to a balcony or external landing must have the balcony/landing built; if the site area is 'NOT built (no outline)', the door is a door into the air and the build stage must either build the landing or flag the door as unresolved.

a door read from a line in an outer wall.rule: A door read from a line in an outer wall at a level above the finished ground (z > 0.30 m) with no stair, ramp, landing or balcony outline reaching it is a misread: it is a window or a high opening, not a door; the reading must not emit a door for an outer-wall opening that no circulation reaches.

when the section prints the ground floor.rule: When the section prints the ground floor at a non-zero mark (e.g. +0.50), the reading must offset every relative level mark in the plans by that amount so that the building's z=0 matches the section's ground-floor mark; otherwise all relative marks are read 0.50 m lower.

an outer-wall opening that is fully or m.rule: An outer-wall opening that is fully or mostly blocked by furniture and has no outside access is a window, not a door; the reading must classify it by its approach, not its width.

when two built pieces overlap and single.rule: When two built pieces overlap and single-piece fixes are exhausted, the furniture agent must re-solve the room's set to resolve the clash.

a built piece covering a window opening.rule: A built piece covering a window opening is a real fit defect; the furniture agent must re-place the piece to clear the opening.

the big loop must run at least one full.rule: The big loop must run at least one full cycle before stopping; a deadline stop with 0 cycles and 303 open major points indicates the loop did not do its job.

views marked for review must be resolved.rule: Views marked for review must be resolved before the run ends; a view that shows a bare wall or a broken scene must be moved or removed.

the exterior scene must be photorealisti.rule: The exterior scene must be photorealistic; low-poly 'lollipop' trees and flat green planes are not acceptable for client-ready renders.

a washbasin model must have style and de.rule: A washbasin model must have style and design detail; a generic, featureless model makes the room look cheap and unfinished.

a kitchen counter must have handles, a p.rule: A kitchen counter must have handles, a proper countertop material, and a sense of a finished appliance run; a plain, featureless white box is not acceptable.

a kitchen must have a coherent run with.rule: A kitchen must have a coherent run with a hob, wall cabinets, and upper storage; a bare slab with a freestanding sink is not acceptable.

a fridge in a minimalist kitchen must ta.rule: A fridge in a minimalist kitchen must take a library model with a visible finish (stainless or panel), never the untextured parametric kitchen-run mesh.

a kitchen render must show a finished ru.rule: A kitchen render must show a finished run (handles, backsplash, appliances) and a dining set in one style; a grey-box massing with a mismatched chair is not client-ready.

a dining chair must match the table's li.rule: A dining chair must match the table's light-wood minimalist style; a dark heavy wooden chair is a style clash.

a stair must be built with a detailed mo.rule: A stair must be built with a detailed model (treads, stringers, handrail), never the untextured parametric solid block; the parametric stair is a placeholder that fails any client render.

a living room must read as one designed.rule: A living room must read as one designed set (matching sofas, chairs, table); a showroom of unrelated styles and a missing dining set is not client-ready.

an armchair in a minimalist salon must m.rule: An armchair in a minimalist salon must match the sofa's style and palette; a loud mid-century egg chair is a style clash.
An armchair in a minimalist salon must match the sofa's style and palette; a black mid-century shell chair is a style clash.

a sofa in a minimalist salon must match.rule: A sofa in a minimalist salon must match the other seating's style and palette; a long low orange sofa is a style clash.

a living room with two facing sofas must.rule: A living room with two facing sofas must have a coffee table or anchor between them and both sofas in one style; a caramel leather and a beige mid-century sofa facing each other with no anchor is not client-ready.

a dining table in a minimalist salon mus.rule: A dining table in a minimalist salon must match the room's light-wood style; a heavy wooden bench is a style clash.

the exterior landscape seen through wind.rule: The exterior landscape seen through windows must be a realistic, textured environment (real trees, hedge, path), never a low-poly lollipop placeholder.

a living room must read as one designed.rule: A living room must read as one designed set; a chaotic mix of styles and scales is not client-ready.

the exterior landscape seen through wind.rule: The exterior landscape seen through windows must be a realistic, textured environment, never a low-poly cartoon placeholder.

a washbasin in a monochromatic white bat.rule: A washbasin in a monochromatic white bathroom must match the room's palette; a stark glossy black box is a style clash.

a bathtub must be built with a detailed.rule: A bathtub must be built with a detailed model (curved rim, texture), never a plain white box primitive.

a bedroom with two beds must have both b.rule: A bedroom with two beds must have both beds in one style and the room composed with clear circulation; a white ornate metal frame and a plain modern frame are a style clash, and a camera too low and too close makes the room read as cluttered.

a room's furniture set must share one st.rule: A room's furniture set must share one style family; when two pieces of the same type in one room are from different style families, swap the one that is the outlier to a model from the family the rest of the room uses.

a wardrobe model must show visible doors.rule: A wardrobe model must show visible doors and hardware; a flat slab-like model with no front detail is not client-ready and must be swapped for a model with a finished front face.

an interior camera must frame the room's.rule: An interior camera must frame the room's main furniture, not a railing, wall or door handle; if the current pose shows a non-furniture element in the foreground, re-aim it at the room's key pieces.
An interior camera must frame the room's main fixtures, not a wall, door handle or shower screen; if the current pose is blocked by a fixture, re-aim it to show the room's contents.

the outdoor environment visible through.rule: The outdoor environment visible through windows must be a believable landscape, not a low-poly placeholder; if the site has fewer than 6 trees or a flat untextured ground, increase the tree count and set a textured ground.

an interior camera must frame the room's.rule: An interior camera must frame the room's main furniture, not a bare wall; if the room reads as a grey-box placeholder, re-aim the camera to show the key pieces.
An interior camera must frame the room's main furniture, not a bare wall; if the room reads as a half-finished shell, re-aim the camera to show the key pieces.

interior doors must match the room's woo.rule: Interior doors must match the room's wood tone; a darker, rawer wood door in a light-oak room clashes and must be set to a matching light wood look.

an interior camera must frame the room's.rule: An interior camera must frame the room's main features, not a blank wall; if the current pose wastes the frame on a wall and door, re-aim it at the room's key elements.
An interior camera must frame the room's contents, not a bare corridor ending on a door; if the room is a small hall, re-aim the camera to show its furniture.

exterior and window views must show a fi.rule: Exterior and window views must show a finished landscape (varied trees, hedge, path) and a textured ground, never the default low-poly placeholder set.

a bed model must include bedding and tex.rule: A bed model must include bedding and texture; a plain slab model is a placeholder and must be swapped for a styled one of the same type and size class.

a wardrobe model must show doors, handle.rule: A wardrobe model must show doors, handles and seams; a flat handle-less slab is a placeholder and must be swapped for a detailed model of the same type.

an interior camera must frame the room's.rule: An interior camera must frame the room's main group, not be pressed against a single piece; the show list must include the room's key pieces.

two wardrobes in the same room must form.rule: Two wardrobes in the same room must form a coherent set (matching style, handles, finish); a mismatched model must be swapped for one that matches its partner.

a decor item that cannot rest on its hos.rule: A decor item that cannot rest on its host (penetration > 0.03 m) must be re-placed or removed in the next furniture round; it must not be left unbuilt.

a soft decor item (cushion, throw) that.rule: A soft decor item (cushion, throw) that cannot rest on its host within the penetration tolerance is dropped, not built floating; it is a minor cosmetic loss, not a missing element.

a sanitary fixture whose library model i.rule: A sanitary fixture whose library model is a plain untextured box should be swapped to a textured model of the same footprint to avoid the 'grey box' look in renders.

a fridge that is built as a sub-part of.rule: A fridge that is built as a sub-part of a kitchen_counter module and is not visible as a distinct appliance should be swapped to a standalone fridge model of the same footprint.

an exterior view that shows a flat empty.rule: An exterior view that shows a flat empty field with placeholder lollipop trees should have site items (trees, path, hedge) added to give the environment depth and realism.

an armchair pushed tight against a wall.rule: An armchair pushed tight against a wall with no breathing room should be re-laid out to give it clearance and a companion piece, so it reads as part of a seating arrangement.

a bed whose decor (pillows, throw) looks.rule: A bed whose decor (pillows, throw) looks unnatural or messy should be swapped to a model with better integrated styling.

a bed with plain, unstyled bedding shoul.rule: A bed with plain, unstyled bedding should be swapped to a model with richer integrated styling (throw, layered pillows) to read as a finished bedroom.

a camera view that does not show the mai.rule: A camera view that does not show the main furniture of a room should be moved to show them, so the room does not feel empty.

a ground that is a flat untextured plane.rule: A ground that is a flat untextured plane should be given a textured look (grass, paving, gravel) to give it realism.

a facade that is a flat untextured white.rule: A facade that is a flat untextured white surface should be given a textured look (plaster, brick, stone) to give it realism.

a stone cladding that is a flat untextur.rule: A stone cladding that is a flat untextured decal should be given a textured stone look to give it realism.

a drawn piece that is left out as a deta.rule: A drawn piece that is left out as a detail of a larger piece but whose size and AI naming fit a standalone furniture type should be retyped to that type so it is built.

the reading stage must read attdef entit.rule: The reading stage must read ATTDEF entities in DWG files, as they often hold room labels, dimensions, or other metadata needed for the model.

when a plan layer is named for a sanitar.rule: When a plan layer is named for a sanitary fixture (e.g. 'DENIZLIK' = washbasin) and its entities are not used by the model, the reading must map that layer to the corresponding fixture type and verify it against the built sanitary pieces, instead of leaving the layer unaccounted for.

when an opening is read twice (duplicate.rule: When an opening is read twice (duplicate) and the build stage cannot place it, the build stage must resolve the duplicate by keeping one instance at the read position rather than dropping the opening entirely.

a movable piece (armchair, sofa, table).rule: A movable piece (armchair, sofa, table) placed by the layout solver is not a misread of a drawn element; offset findings on movable pieces are layout noise, not reading errors, and should not be treated as misreads.

interior doors at the same floor level o.rule: Interior doors at the same floor level on both sides correctly have no threshold; a flush door leaf is the expected geometry, not a defect.

subjective aesthetic critiques of exteri.rule: Subjective aesthetic critiques of exterior composition (railing placement, flow) are not model errors; they are render/staging opinions that do not require a geometry fix.

balcony railing style and minor visual g.rule: Balcony railing style and minor visual gaps are aesthetic choices, not geometry errors; they do not require a model fix unless the railing is missing or structurally incomplete.

a room with an area below 3 m2 and no fu.rule: A room with an area below 3 m2 and no furniture or fixtures is a storage/utility space, not a hall; the reading stage should type small unlabeled rooms as storage by default.

a room with an area below 4 m2 and no fu.rule: A room with an area below 4 m2 and no furniture or fixtures is a storage/utility space, not a hall; the reading stage should type small unlabeled rooms as storage by default.

the reading stage must extract the north.rule: The reading stage must extract the north arrow (or equivalent orientation mark) from the drawing and use it to assign a bearing to each elevation, so that elevation-to-plan checks can run.

the reading stage must verify that a dra.rule: The reading stage must verify that a drawn section's cut line aligns with the plan's roof outline (within 0.30 m) before the section-to-roof check runs; if they do not align, the section is flagged as misread and the check is skipped with a clear reason.
the reading stage must verify that a dra.target: the drawn section r# is not checked point by point against the roof

the reading stage must extract the north.rule: The reading stage must extract the north arrow and assign a bearing to every elevation; elevations without a bearing are flagged as unread and excluded from the model comparison with a clear reason.

a dressing room smaller than 8 m2 does n.rule: A dressing room smaller than 8 m2 does not need a full dressing group (vanity, mirror, seating); a wardrobe is sufficient for the room's function, and the layout solver is correct to skip the group when it does not fit.

when no library model fits a window's di.rule: When no library model fits a window's dimensions, the parametric opening in the style's finish is the correct fallback; this is a library gap, not a model error, and should not be flagged as a defect.

when a kitchen fixture is built parametr.rule: When a kitchen fixture is built parametrically because no library model fits, the fit stage should check for a close-size library model (within 10% of the drawn size) and use it if available, to avoid the 'below library level' warning.

when no library model fits a wall cabine.rule: When no library model fits a wall cabinet's dimensions, the parametric cabinet is the correct fallback; this is a library gap, not a model error, and should not be flagged as a defect.

when a dining table is built with a low-.rule: When a dining table is built with a low-poly or untextured model, the fit stage should prefer a library model with visible base detail and texture, even if it is slightly larger than the drawn size, to avoid the 'crude geometry' warning.

a living room's seating set carries one.rule: A living room's seating set carries one coffee table; a second identical table in the same zone is clutter, not a program, and is removed.

sanitary fixtures in a finished bathroom.rule: Sanitary fixtures in a finished bathroom take a minimal/modern catalogue model, not a generic default.

wet-room walls take a tile or stone look.rule: Wet-room walls take a tile or stone look, never a flat untextured white plaster.

the exterior site carries real trees and.rule: The exterior site carries real trees and a finished ground, not lollipop placeholders on a washed-out plane.

a bathroom camera frames the fixtures it.rule: A bathroom camera frames the fixtures it is meant to show; a view dominated by a glass screen that hides the toilet is re-aimed at the fixtures.

every fixture in a small bathroom must b.rule: Every fixture in a small bathroom must be fully in frame; a cut-off washbasin means the camera is re-aimed to include it.

a shower model must show its head and co.rule: A shower model must show its head and controls, not just a glass panel and wall.

a master bedroom bed takes a styled cata.rule: A master bedroom bed takes a styled catalogue model with headboard and bedding, not a bare low-profile platform.

two armchairs placed as a pair must be t.rule: Two armchairs placed as a pair must be the same model or a deliberately coordinated set.

a floor lamp in a soft-palette seating c.rule: A floor lamp in a soft-palette seating corner takes a low, warm model, not a tall slender tripod that overpowers the chairs.

a double bed's sleeping set carries a ni.rule: A double bed's sleeping set carries a nightstand on each side; a single nightstand with empty wall on the other side is a missing piece.

interior doors take a finished wood or p.rule: Interior doors take a finished wood or painted look, not a plain flat slab.

a nightstand in a calm, finished bedroom.rule: A nightstand in a calm, finished bedroom takes a styled catalogue model, not a plain open box.

window frames on a composed facade take.rule: Window frames on a composed facade take a warm wood or painted look, not identical narrow white plastic units.

outdoor furniture (veranda/terrace seati.rule: Outdoor furniture (veranda/terrace seating) takes a styled catalogue model in the project's exterior style, not a generic default 3D model.

an opening read twice from the documents.rule: An opening read twice from the documents and named in the evidence must be built; the build stage must not drop a double-read opening.

axis/grid bubbles and their labels are d.rule: Axis/grid bubbles and their labels are drawing annotations and are never built as building elements.

cushions and pillows drawn on a piece ar.rule: Cushions and pillows drawn on a piece are details of that piece and are not built as separate furniture.

cushions/pillows already part of a libra.rule: Cushions/pillows already part of a library model are not added again from the drawing.

columns drawn for a veranda/terrace are.rule: Columns drawn for a veranda/terrace are built as its posts, not as separate interior elements.

level/contour marks are drawing annotati.rule: Level/contour marks are drawing annotations and are never built as building elements.

exterior area labels are annotations; th.rule: Exterior area labels are annotations; their surfaces are built from the site paving/grass, not as separate elements.

a single drawn object read twice is buil.rule: A single drawn object read twice is built once, not as two pieces.

a piece drawn inside another piece (>=60.rule: A piece drawn inside another piece (>=60% overlap) is a part of it, not a separate piece.

a kitchen run drawn as one outline with.rule: A kitchen run drawn as one outline with its fixtures is built as its counter legs along the walls, not as one block.

an outline enclosing a group of pieces i.rule: An outline enclosing a group of pieces is a rug/zone outline, not a furniture piece.

a piece removed by the ai must be re-add.rule: A piece removed by the AI must be re-added if the room's program still requires it.

a drawn cluster larger than 4.5 m on a s.rule: A drawn cluster larger than 4.5 m on a side is a group of pieces and must be resolved into its constituents, not left untyped.

a drawn mark thinner than 0.2 m on a sid.rule: A drawn mark thinner than 0.2 m on a side is a line (threshold, shelf, valve), not a piece: it is not built and is not a loss.

a drawn element 60% or more inside anoth.rule: A drawn element 60% or more inside another built piece is a detail of that piece, not a piece of its own: it is not built and is not a loss.

a nightstand drawn beside a bed that ove.rule: A nightstand drawn beside a bed that overlaps it must be re-placed in the free space at the bed's head, not dropped.

a piece removed by the ai's remove_piece.rule: A piece removed by the AI's remove_piece decision is not a loss; the conservation check records it as not built by design.

a stair's upper landing on the top floor.rule: A stair's upper landing on the top floor is not a separate piece; it is the same stair and is not built again.

a decor item whose host piece is not bui.rule: A decor item whose host piece is not built is not built either; it is a consequence of the host's absence, not an independent loss.

a door symbol on a drawing layer (kapi).rule: A door symbol on a drawing layer (KAPI) is an annotation, not a built door; it is not built and is not a loss.

hatch entities on annotation layers (tar.rule: Hatch entities on annotation layers (TARAMA, HATCH) are drawing symbols, not built geometry; they are never built and their absence is not a loss.

outdoor space details (edges, steps) tha.rule: Outdoor space details (edges, steps) that are built as part of a larger outdoor space element are not lost; the finding is a false alarm when the element is accounted for in the built space.

a consistent offset between the building.rule: A consistent offset between the building frame and the sheet outline is a coordinate datum, not an error; it is informational only.

when a section shows the ground floor at.rule: When a section shows the ground floor at a non-zero printed level (e.g. +0.50), the reading stage must apply that offset to all plan level marks so that relative heights (sills, thresholds, fixture working heights) are correct in the model.

small drawn pieces adjacent to level-mar.rule: Small drawn pieces adjacent to level-mark text are level-mark symbols, not furniture; they are correctly excluded from the build.

a furniture name text in the documents i.rule: A furniture name text in the documents is satisfied when the named piece type is already present in the room; no additional action is needed.

when a document-named piece cannot be pl.rule: When a document-named piece cannot be placed within the tolerance of its text label due to room geometry, the finding is a placement constraint, not a loss; it is handled by the placement solver.

a zone label in the documents is satisfi.rule: A zone label in the documents is satisfied when the corresponding furniture type is present in the room; no additional action is needed.

when a document-named piece cannot be pl.rule: When a document-named piece cannot be placed within tolerance of its text label, the furniture agent should attempt to place it at the nearest valid spot even if slightly beyond the text tolerance, rather than omitting it entirely.

when a drawn opening is blocked by a dra.rule: When a drawn opening is blocked by a drawn piece such that it cannot function as a door, and the opening's dimensions match a window (sill height, width), it should be read as a window, not a door.

a window (sill >= 0.90 m) in an outer wa.rule: A window (sill >= 0.90 m) in an outer wall is not a passage; furniture standing in front of it is not a blocked door and does not need a walkway.

furniture must not block the approach to.rule: Furniture must not block the approach to a door or window in a way that prevents its use.

a hall smaller than 3 m² does not requir.rule: A hall smaller than 3 m² does not require furniture.

furniture must not overlap other furnitu.rule: Furniture must not overlap other furniture.

furniture must not cover a window..rule: Furniture must not cover a window.

a labelled site area (veranda, balcony,.rule: A labelled site area (veranda, balcony, terrace) must be built as a platform with its own floor and edge, even if its surface is partially covered by the main building footprint.

a site area labelled 'veranda' or 'balko.rule: A site area labelled 'VERANDA' or 'BALKON' in the documents must be built as a covered or open terrace with a floor and a railing, not omitted or replaced by a flat roof.

a dressing room (soyunma odası) must be.rule: A dressing room (soyunma odası) must be adjacent to and accessible from a bedroom or bathroom, not a standalone room.

a room labelled 'oda' (room) that is sma.rule: A room labelled 'Oda' (room) that is smaller than 4 m2 and contains only a shoe cabinet should be typed as 'storage' or 'other', not 'hall'.

a hall on an upper floor must be connect.rule: A hall on an upper floor must be connected to the stair and to the rooms it serves. It should not be a dead-end.

a bathroom must be accessible from a hal.rule: A bathroom must be accessible from a hall or a bedroom. It should not be a dead-end.

a bedroom must be connected to a bathroo.rule: A bedroom must be connected to a bathroom or a hall that leads to a bathroom.
